q: Does a direct raw-read short-vs-long assembly comparison on this dataset (MiSeq SPAdes vs MinION CANU/Flye) actually reproduce the paper's claimed AMR/plasmid-dropout advantage, and if so at what gene-count-delta and misassembly rate?
basis: The paper's central METHODOLOGICAL thesis (long-read recovers genes short-read misses) was NOT directly tested in this replication — we used the deposited PacBio-based CP assemblies as ground truth. Our AMR/virulome/plasmid architecture reproduction merely supports the paper's biology, not its methods argument.
next_steps: On uicgpu: (a) download SRR8335317 (MinION 3.5 GB), SRR8335318 + SRR8333590/91/92 (MiSeq); (b) assemble MinION with CANU (or Flye) + short-read polish (Racon+Pilon); (c) assemble MiSeq alone with SPAdes; (d) re-run abricate on both assemblies and count AMR/virulence gene recovery vs the CP ground truth; (e) tabulate per-gene: present in long-read?, present in short-read?, misassembled?; (f) publish delta and check against paper's specific claims about which genes short-read missed. Expected wall-clock: 4-8 h.

q: Do the paper's PHASTER prophage counts/sizes (Table 8) reproduce on the deposited CP assemblies, and specifically do the Stx-phage genomic-island boundaries + insertion sites agree once genome-origin rotation is normalized?
basis: This replication reproduced Stx-phage TYPE (1a/1a/2a) and chromosomal localization but explicitly deferred prophage counts and boundary coordinates because the paper's coordinates are in a different origin-rotated frame. This leaves a real testable gap.
next_steps: Run PHASTER (or PHASTEST) on the three CP chromosomes CP037941/CP037944/CP037946. Re-rotate all three assemblies to dnaA-start frame using dnaapler or manual identification. Compare (a) prophage count per genome vs paper Table 8, (b) prophage sizes, (c) Stx-phage integration site coordinates in the rotated frame. Report concordance % and identify any phages 'lost' or 'added' by different tooling.

q: What is the mobilization potential and host range of the 73 kb IncFII AMR plasmid in CFSAN027346, and does the tmexCD3-toprJ3 / blaTEM-1B / sul2 / tetB / dfrA8 cluster represent an epidemiologically significant conjugative element in the STEC or broader Enterobacteriaceae population?
basis: The paper (and this replication) confirms all AMR genes sit on a 73 kb plasmid but neither work directly analyzes its transfer machinery, oriT, relaxase, or population prevalence. The clinical narrative implicitly depends on transferability.
next_steps: For CP037947 (73 kb plasmid): (a) run oriTfinder + MOB-suite to identify relaxase family, oriT, mating-pair-formation systems; (b) run PlasmidFinder for full Inc typing; (c) mash-screen against NCBI RefSeq plasmid database to find nearest cognates and infer host range; (d) BLAST the concrete AMR-gene composition against enterobase.warwick.ac.uk STEC surveillance metadata to see if this exact plasmid backbone has been observed elsewhere. Report whether this is a novel plasmid or a member of a known circulating lineage.

q: How should genome-origin choice be standardized across STEC studies so that phage coordinates and other feature positions are directly comparable, and does this affect any biological interpretations?
basis: The Stx-phage coordinate mismatch between paper Table 8 and this replication (§4.6 in REPORT.md) is a pure origin-rotation artifact. This is a recurring cross-study reproducibility friction that ONLY affects presentation but bites automated pipelines.
next_steps: (a) Survey the STEC literature and 20 recent GenBank complete-genome deposits to see what fraction rotate to dnaA-start vs other conventions. (b) Implement dnaapler-based re-rotation on the CP037941/44/46 chromosomes and re-derive all feature coordinates. (c) Propose a community standard (probably dnaA-start-forward-strand) and quantify how many current STEC deposits comply. (d) Publish a normalized coordinate map file that any downstream re-analysis can use to translate paper coordinates ↔ standardized coordinates.

q: Are Nanopore-only assemblies (without PacBio or short-read polishing) sufficient to accurately close STEC O26 genomes, especially at hard regions like Stx-phage integration sites, IS-element clusters, and repetitive rRNA operons — and if so, does this change the cost/benefit calculus for outbreak investigation?
basis: This paper used MinION + PacBio + MiSeq (three technologies). The methodological thesis is 'long-read recovers what short-read misses' but the paper does not isolate MinION-only performance. If MinION-alone is sufficient, that would radically change field-deployable outbreak sequencing economics.
next_steps: On uicgpu: assemble SRR8335317 (MinION only, with modern basecaller e.g. Dorado sup-mode) with (a) Flye and (b) miniasm+Racon+Medaka polish only. Compare against the CP ground truth for: (i) chromosome closure Y/N, (ii) plasmid recovery count (should be 1/2/1), (iii) Stx-phage integration site consensus accuracy, (iv) IS-element resolution, (v) rRNA operon count/copy-number, (vi) AMR gene call accuracy at 100% identity threshold. Report a decision matrix: at what Nanopore coverage + basecaller model does MinION-only match hybrid?
